title: Why I document architecture decisions.
excerpt: Good code explains what happens. Good documentation explains why.

sections.title: The problem with undocumented decisions
paragraphs: Imagine joining a software team and discovering that nobody knows why an important architectural decision was made. The code tells you how the system works, but rarely why it was designed that way.
This is why understanding and documenting technical decisions matters.

sections.title: Making decisions visible
paragraphs: An architecture decision record captures the context around a choice, the options considered and the reason a team moved forward with one of them.
Keeping the record short and close to the code makes it easier for the next person to understand the trade-offs.

sections.title: Trade-offs are part of the story
paragraphs: Most engineering choices solve one problem while creating constraints elsewhere. Writing those constraints down helps teams revisit a decision when the context changes.

title: Another Perspective on System Design
excerpt: A practical look at the questions that make system design clearer.

sections.title: Start with the problem
paragraphs: System design gets easier when the user needs, constraints and expected scale are clear before choosing technologies.

sections.title: Make trade-offs explicit
paragraphs: There is rarely one perfect architecture. A useful design explains what it optimizes for and what it makes harder.

sections.title: Design for change
paragraphs: Prefer clear boundaries that let the system evolve as requirements become better understood.

title: Building my own monitoring platform.
excerpt: Designing a system that understands dependencies and service health.

sections.title: Start with a small signal
paragraphs: A useful monitoring platform starts with a focused question: what needs attention, and how quickly should someone know?

sections.title: Make the data reliable
paragraphs: Collection, storage and alerting each need clear failure behavior so missing data does not look like a healthy system.

sections.title: Iterate from real use
paragraphs: Dashboards and alerts become more useful when they are shaped by the decisions people need to make.

title: Just because it works doesnt mean it works well.
excerpt: Engineering responsibility in an AI-assisted world.

sections.title: Working is a starting point
paragraphs: A passing result can still hide fragile assumptions, unclear behavior or code that is difficult to maintain.

sections.title: Review the result
paragraphs: AI-assisted work still needs engineering judgment: verify the behavior, understand the changes and check how they fit the system.

sections.title: Own the outcome
paragraphs: The person shipping the change is responsible for its quality, whether the first draft came from a person or a tool.

title: Designing a better deployment workflow.
excerpt: Exploring self-hosting, Docker and deployment practices.

sections.title: Finding the friction
paragraphs: A deployment workflow should make it clear what is being released, where it is going and how to recover if something goes wrong.

sections.title: Make releases repeatable
paragraphs: Containerizing the app and keeping configuration outside the image helps the same release move across environments.

sections.title: Improve one step at a time
paragraphs: Automating the most repetitive or error-prone steps first keeps the workflow understandable as it grows.
